beats.text: A 22 year old at British intelligence found it first, in 1973.
beats.note: The public inventors, Rivest, Shamir and Adleman, published in 1977.

beats.name: Clifford Cocks
beats.role: Joined GCHQ's CESG in September. His surviving note is dated 20 November.

beats.lead: The idea came from a colleague
beats.text: Nick Patterson told him about James Ellis's "non-secret encryption".
beats.note: Ellis had the concept but no way to make it work.

beats.text: The work stayed classified for 24 years.
beats.note: Cocks spoke about it publicly on 18 December 1997.

beats.text: The internet's lock existed before the internet needed one.
